text:
The page is a product listing for the ALLPOWERS R4000, not a power station and solar panel combo guide. It doesn't name or recommend any solar panels, so it doesn't back up "best combo for an RV".

**Price and codes** (tested by Dealectric in ALLPOWERS's cart, Oct 23–24)
- **Store price:** $1,499 (the page lists $3,299 as the "list" price).
- **EXTRA12:** 12% off orders over $1,200, which brings it to **$1,319.12**. It expires Nov 15.
- **ALLPOWERS26 or EXTRA10:** 10% off, which brings it to $1,349.10. The ALLPOWERS26 test was run on a different product (the P1800), so its saving on the R4000 is calculated, not tested.
- The checkout usually takes only one code per order.

**Specs**
- **Battery:** 3,456 Wh LiFePO4, rated for 3,500+ cycles.
- **AC output:** 3,600 W continuous at 120 V, with a 6,000 W peak. The 4,000 W in the title is the 230 V rating, so it doesn't apply to US outlets. It has an RV outlet.
- **Solar input:** up to 2,000 W across 3 XT60 inputs. Each input takes 650 W at 12–60 V. You need panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000 W.
- **AC recharge:** about 2 hours.
- **Weight:** 45 kg (99 lb), so you can't carry it by hand. Plan where it will sit in the RV.
- **Warranty:** 5 years.

**Things to watch**
- Returns are 30 days for unused items in the original package, and you pay return shipping unless the unit is defective. ALLPOWERS's refund page also says sale items can't be returned.
- The site is an affiliate and earns a commission if you buy through its link. The prices and code tests are still useful, but check the final price at checkout.

For an RV, I'd pick panels sized to your roof space and match their voltage and wattage to the 12–60 V, 650 W-per-input limits. I can look for specific panels if you'd like.

**Buy link:** [ALLPOWERS R4000 at ALLPOWERS's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link. Enter EXTRA12 at checkout.
